The complete glossary of ad and creative intelligence terminology
Tomas Hubka
Last updated: Sep 03, 2026
min read
A complete glossary of ad and creative intelligence terminology for mobile games. Definitions of every term UA and creative teams need to know in 2026.
Ad intelligence, creative intelligence, and mobile user acquisition have their own vocabulary. Some of the terms are used loosely across the industry, some mean different things in different platforms, and some are new enough that even experienced UA managers hedge their definitions. This glossary is a working reference for the terms that show up most often in mobile UA, creative research, and competitive analysis conversations in 2026.
Terms are grouped by category. Where a term has a direct product feature or documentation counterpart, we've linked out.
Ad and creative intelligence foundations
Ad intelligence
: The practice of collecting, analyzing, and acting on data about advertising activity across the market. For mobile games, that means understanding which studios are advertising, where they're advertising, how much they're spending, what creatives they're running, and who they're targeting. See our
complete guide to ad intelligence
.
Creative intelligence
: The subset of ad intelligence focused specifically on the advertising creatives themselves. What the ads look like, what patterns connect the winners, how they evolve over time, and how top studios structure their creative production. See our
complete guide to creative intelligence
.
Market intelligence
: The broader category covering everything about a market beyond ads. Downloads, revenue, DAU, retention, category share, top charts, and market movement. Often used interchangeably with market research.
Competitive intelligence
: A general term for research into competitor activity across every dimension of their business, including advertising, monetization, product, and organization.
Ad tracking
: The continuous monitoring of ad creatives, ad networks, and campaign activity. In the context of ad intelligence tools, this usually means tracking what competitors are running, not tracking your own campaigns.
Creative research
: The disciplined practice of studying ads in market to inform your own creative decisions. Overlaps heavily with creative intelligence, but often refers to the human workflow rather than the tool that supports it.
Ad Insights
: GameAnalytics' ad and creative intelligence platform. Combines ad intelligence, creative intelligence, and market signals in a single workflow. See the
Ad Insights overview
.
Ad creative types and formats
Video ad
: An ad that plays a video clip. The dominant format across mobile game UA in 2026, typically ranging from 6 seconds to 60 seconds.
Playable ad
: An interactive ad that lets the user play a short version of the game inside the ad unit. Higher production cost, but consistently strong performance for aligning UA with actual gameplay.
Image ad
: A static banner, tile, or full-screen image ad. Less common in mobile game UA than video, but still used across banner placements and store spots.
Interstitial ad
: A full-screen ad that appears between content transitions, typically in mobile games. Can be video, image, or playable.
Banner ad
: A small ad placement, typically at the top or bottom of the screen. Lower CPM than interstitials or rewarded, still used for continuous impression volume.
Rewarded video
: A video ad that gives the player an in-game reward in exchange for watching. Some of the highest engagement rates in mobile advertising because the player opts in.
End card
: The static or interactive screen that appears at the end of a video ad, usually containing the install CTA. Often the most-optimized element of a video ad.
Web-to-app (W2A)
: A campaign type that drives users to a web landing page first, then to the app store. Common in creative-heavy strategies where the landing page enables extra targeting, testing, or storytelling.
App Store Redirect
: A campaign type that drives users directly to the app store listing from an ad.
